Basant Maheshwari.philosophy: Pay up for real quality growth only when high ROE is backed by genuine cash flow and a solid balance sheet, not paper profits.
Basant Maheshwari.thesis: The "3B" filter — pay up for real quality growth only if the cash flows and balance sheet actually back it; skip anything trading below face value or paying zero dividend (proxy for a stock the market has given up on). High ROE plus real (not paper) profit via positive operating cash flow and free cash flow, a hard solvency floor (interest coverage), and Piotroski score as a sanity check.
Basant Maheshwari.exit: Exit if: Operating cash flow < Net profit for 2 consecutive years (earnings quality slipping) · ROE < 18 · Interest Coverage Ratio < 3 · Promoter holding declines for 3 consecutive quarters · stop-loss at -20% from entry.
Basant Maheshwari.screen:
Return on equity > 25 AND
 Sales growth 3Years > 25 AND
 Cash from operations last year > 0 AND
 Free cash flow last year > 0 AND
 Interest Coverage Ratio > 3 AND
 Promoter holding > 40 AND
 Piotroski score > 3 AND
 Current ratio > 1 AND
 Current price > 100

Buffett.philosophy: Own durable-moat businesses with high, stable long-run returns on capital and low debt, bought at a reasonable price.
Buffett.thesis: Durable competitive moat, high and stable long-run returns on capital, minimal debt — buy a wonderful business at a fair price and hold indefinitely. 5-year average ROE/ROCE (not just TTM) proves durability; the Graham-Buffett hybrid ceiling (8.5 + 2×growth) caps what a "fair price" means numerically.
Buffett.exit: Exit if: Average ROE 5Years < 12 · Debt to equity > 0.7 · OPM compresses more than 400bps for 2 consecutive years (pricing power lost) · Price to Earning exceeds the growth-implied ceiling by more than 50%.
Buffett.screen:
Return on equity > 15 AND
 Average return on equity 5Years > 15 AND
 Return on capital employed > 15 AND
 Average return on capital employed 5Years > 15 AND
 Debt to equity < 0.5 AND
 Interest Coverage Ratio > 8 AND
 OPM 5Year > 15 AND
 Sales growth 5Years > 8 AND
 Profit growth 5Years > 8 AND
 Promoter holding > 50 AND
 Price to Earning < (8.5 + 2 * Profit growth 5Years) AND
 Price to book value < 4

CANSLIM.philosophy: Buy stocks with strong current/annual earnings acceleration making fresh highs on strength, not weakness, with market-direction confirmation.
CANSLIM.thesis: Current and annual earnings acceleration plus a fresh 52-week high on rising volume, with market-direction confirmation — buy strength, not weakness. O'Neil's 7-factor CANSLIM checklist verified against his published criteria. This is the one style genuinely native to Chartink (price/volume-driven) — kept mostly technical with a thin earnings-acceleration fundamental gate. On Screener.in (no volume/SMA engine) the breakout leg is approximated with DMA 50/200 fields.
CANSLIM.exit: Exit if: Close falls below the 50-day SMA (Chartink) / DMA 50 (Screener) on above-average volume · next quarterly EPS misses YoY · hard stop-loss at -7% to -8% from purchase price (O'Neil's own published rule).
CANSLIM.screen:
Current price > DMA 50 AND
 DMA 50 > DMA 200 AND
 Current price >= 0.95 * High price AND [proxy for 52-week-high proximity]
 EPS latest quarter > EPS preceding quarter AND
 EPS latest quarter > EPS preceding year quarter AND
 Profit growth 3Years > 20 AND
 Return on equity > 17 AND
 Volume 1week average > 1.5 * Volume 1month average

Cathie Wood.philosophy: High-conviction idea funnel on exponential-growth, TAM-expansion themes, prioritizing accelerating revenue growth over near-term profitability; not a value/quality core.
Cathie Wood.thesis: High-conviction bets on exponential-growth themes — revenue growth and TAM expansion over near-term profitability. Explicitly not a value or quality screen; treat output purely as an idea funnel, not a portfolio core. Very high, accelerating top-line growth is the only reliable signal on Indian disclosure data; profitability and leverage checks are deliberately loose or absent, matching the style's actual risk profile.
Cathie Wood.exit: Exit if: quarterly sales growth decelerates below 15% · hard stop-loss at -25% from entry (deliberately wide given no valuation floor) · position size capped at 3-5% of portfolio given the volatility.
Cathie Wood.screen:
Sales growth 3Years > 30 AND
 YOY Quarterly sales growth > 25 AND
 Market Capitalization < 20000 AND
 Market Capitalization > 500 AND
 Volume 1week average > 2 * Volume 1month average

Coffee Can (Marcellus).philosophy: Buy-and-forget large, high-ROCE compounders that have grown consistently for a decade-plus, not just averaged well.
Coffee Can (Marcellus).thesis: Buy-and-forget portfolio of businesses that have compounded ROCE and revenue every single year for a decade-plus — the differentiator versus generic "quality" screens is consistency, not average. Requiring the multi-horizon average (3/5/7/10-year) ROCE and sales growth to all clear the same bar simultaneously is the standard proxy for "every individual year," which cannot be tested year-by-year in a single scan clause.
Coffee Can (Marcellus).exit: Exit if: any single fiscal year's ROCE (check manually against the annual report once a year) < 12 · Debt to equity > 0.5 · Sales growth 3Years average < 5 — this is a multi-year hold, so exit only on genuine consistency breaks, never on price noise alone.

Return on capital employed > 15 AND
 Average return on capital employed 3Years > 15 AND
 Average return on capital employed 5Years > 15 AND
 Average return on capital employed 7Years > 15 AND
 Average return on capital employed 10Years > 15 AND
 Sales growth 3Years > 10 AND
 Sales growth 5Years > 10 AND
 Sales growth 7Years > 10 AND
 Sales growth 10Years > 10 AND
 Debt to equity < 0.3 AND
 Market Capitalization > 1000

Dolly Khanna.philosophy: Buy low-visibility, cheap-on-sales small caps (often agro-chem/commodity-linked) before the market notices them.
Dolly Khanna.thesis: Low-visibility, cheap-on-sales small/mid caps (historically agro-chem and commodity-linked) bought before broad coverage. Price-to-Sales below 1 is the anchor — it survives commodity-cycle earnings volatility far better than P/E; ROCE and promoter holding confirm the cheapness is not for a bad reason.
Dolly Khanna.exit: Exit if: Price to Sales > 2 · Sales growth 3Years < 0 · Promoter holding < 25 · Interest Coverage Ratio < 4 · stop-loss at -25% from entry.
Dolly Khanna.screen:
Market Capitalization > 1000 AND
 Market Capitalization < 8000 AND
 Price to Sales < 1 AND
 Sales growth 3Years > 15 AND
 Profit growth 3Years > 15 AND
 Return on capital employed > 15 AND
 Promoter holding > 30 AND
 Interest Coverage Ratio > 6 AND
 Price to Earning < 25

Dreman.philosophy: Buy fundamentally sound, low-PE, out-of-favor dividend payers where market pessimism, not weak fundamentals, has depressed the price.
Dreman.thesis: Buy low P/E, low P/B, dividend-paying stocks that are fundamentally sound but out of market favor — bet against consensus pessimism, not against the balance sheet. Relative cheapness (PE well below industry norm) plus a payout-ratio ceiling that filters out names paying dividends they cannot actually afford.
Dreman.exit: Exit if: Price to Earning rises above Industry PE (thesis realized) · Dividend Payout Ratio > 70 (dividend at risk) · EPS growth negative for 2 consecutive years.
Dreman.screen:
Price to Earning < 0.6 * Industry PE AND
 Price to book value < 1.5 AND
 Dividend Payout Ratio < 50 AND
 Dividend Payout Ratio > 0 AND
 Current ratio > 1.5 AND
 EPS growth 5Years > 0 AND
 Debt to equity < 0.75

Graham.philosophy: Statistically cheap, financially sound companies bought at a deep discount to a conservatively appraised (Graham formula) intrinsic value.
Graham.thesis: Classic defensive value investing — statistically cheap, financially sound companies bought at a deep discount to conservatively appraised worth. Uses Graham's own verified 1974 revised formula, V = EPS x (8.5 + 2g) x 4.4/Y, as the price ceiling (g = 5-year sales growth as a growth proxy, Y = current long bond yield, ~7 for India) — this corrects the unsourced "(7+g)x6.5/7.9" constant your PDF variant used.
Graham.exit: Exit if: Current price rises above the Graham-formula ceiling value · Current ratio < 1.5 · Debt to equity > 1 · EPS growth negative for 2 consecutive years (the safety margin was illusory).
Graham.screen:
Current price <= EPS preceding year * (8.5 + 2 * Sales growth 5Years) * 4.4 / 7 AND
 Price to Earning < 15 AND
 Price to book value < 1.5 AND
 Current ratio > 2 AND
 Debt to equity < 0.5 AND
 PEG Ratio <= 1 AND
 Average return on equity 5Years > 12 AND
 Free cash flow 5Years > 0 AND
 Market Capitalization > 500

Greenblatt.philosophy: A mechanical basket ranking cheapness (earnings yield) and quality (return on capital) together, rebalanced annually rather than held on conviction.
Greenblatt.thesis: Rank on cheapness (earnings yield) and quality (return on capital) simultaneously — a mechanical, story-agnostic basket approach, rebalanced annually, not a buy-and-hold single-stock style. Uses Greenblatt's own published definitions verified this session: Earnings Yield = EBIT / Enterprise Value; Return on Capital = EBIT / (Net Fixed Assets + Net Working Capital). Rank both, sum the ranks, take the cheapest-plus-highest-quality basket.
Greenblatt.exit: Exit rule (mechanical, not stock-specific): rebalance the ENTIRE basket once every 12 months regardless of individual stock performance — do not hold any single name past its 12-month cycle on conviction; do not sell mid-cycle unless a stock is acquired/delisted.
Greenblatt.screen:
EBIT / Enterprise Value > 0.10 AND
 EBIT / (Net block + Working capital) > 0.25 AND
 Market Capitalization > 500 AND
 Debt to equity < 0.4 AND
 Sales > 30
  
 Export to Excel/Sheets: rank all matches by EBIT/EV (desc) + rank by
 EBIT/(Net block+WC) (desc); sum the two ranks ascending; take the top 20-30.
 Exclude Financials/NBFCs/Utilities manually - EBIT/EV is meaningless for them.

Jhunjhunwala.philosophy: Buy visible, rising growth before full re-rating, favoring rising ROE/ROCE and reasonable PE relative to growth rather than pure value.
Jhunjhunwala.thesis: Growth at a reasonable price with a strong bias toward businesses gaining pricing power and rising promoter conviction — buy visible growth before the market fully re-rates it, then hold for years. High and improving ROE/ROCE, growth outrunning the price paid (PE below Industry PE as a PEG proxy), and promoter stake rising rather than falling — the cleanest quantitative tell that insiders agree with the growth story.
Jhunjhunwala.exit: Exit if: Promoter holding falls QoQ (any decline) · ROE < 15 for 2 consecutive quarters · Price to Earning > 1.3x Industry PE while Profit growth 5Years < 10 · Profit growth YoY < 0 · hard stop-loss at -20% from entry price.
Jhunjhunwala.screen:
Return on equity > 20 AND
 Return on capital employed > 15 AND
 Sales growth 5Years > 12 AND
 Profit growth 5Years > 15 AND
 Price to Earning < Industry PE AND
 Debt to equity < 0.5 AND
 Promoter holding > 35 AND
 Change in promoter holding 3Years > 0 AND
 OPM > 15

John Neff.philosophy: Unloved, low-P/E stocks whose (growth + yield)/PE total-return ratio confirms the cheapness isn't a value trap.
John Neff.thesis: Unloved, low-P/E stocks with decent growth and a real dividend. Neff's own "total return ratio," (growth + yield) / PE, verified against his published low-PE investing framework, is the number that defines the thesis. The formula directly gates entries; ROE and free cash flow confirm the low PE is not a value trap.
John Neff.exit: Exit if: total-return ratio falls below 1 · dividend gets cut (Dividend Yield drops more than 40% YoY) · Price to Earning rises above 20 without matching Profit growth 5Years above 15.
John Neff.screen:
(Profit growth 5Years + Dividend Yield) / Price to Earning > 2 AND
 Price to Earning < 14 AND
 Dividend Yield > 1.5 AND
 Sales growth 5Years > 7 AND
 Return on equity > 15 AND
 Free cash flow 3years > 0 AND
 Pledged percentage = 0

Kacholia.philosophy: Identify niche small/micro-cap leaders with multi-year accelerating growth before institutional discovery.
Kacholia.thesis: Get ahead of institutional discovery — niche small/micro-cap leaders whose earnings growth is accelerating faster than the market has priced in. Multi-horizon growth consistency (3/5-year sales, 3-year profit, ROCE, ROE all clearing the same bar) filters out one-quarter flukes; a capped market cap keeps the universe genuinely small-cap.
Kacholia.exit: Exit if: Market Capitalization > 10,000cr (graduated out of small-cap mandate) · Sales growth 3Years < 10 · Price to Earning > 40 while Profit growth 3Years < 15 · Promoter holding falls QoQ · stop-loss at -25% from entry (small-cap volatility allowance).

Kenneth Fisher.philosophy: Use low, stable Price-to-Sales to find companies with temporarily depressed but structurally intact margins, avoiding P/E distortion from one-off earnings swings.
Kenneth Fisher.thesis: Price-to-Sales is a more stable valuation anchor than P/E because it is not distorted by one-off earnings swings — best applied to companies with temporarily depressed margins that remain structurally intact. Very low P/S (<0.75) plus positive, improving net margins proves depressed earnings are cyclical, not structural.
Kenneth Fisher.exit: Exit if: Price to Sales rises above 1.5 · net profit margin turns negative any single year · Piotroski score < 5.
Kenneth Fisher.screen:
Price to Sales < 0.75 AND
 Debt to equity < 0.4 AND
 Profit growth 5Years > 20 AND
 NPM last year > 3 AND
 NPM preceding year > 3 AND
 Cash from operations last year > 0 AND
 Piotroski score > 6

Mark Minervini.philosophy: SEPA: own technically strong leadership stocks in confirmed uptrends with accelerating earnings/sales growth, buying breakouts from consolidation.

O'Shaughnessy.philosophy: Buy the cheapest quartile on a multi-metric value composite, but only where price trend confirms the market has started to agree with the value case.
O'Shaughnessy.thesis: A multi-factor value composite (not any single cheap ratio) combined with a momentum overlay — buy the cheapest quartile that the market has also started rewarding. Ranking across several valuation metrics avoids single-ratio distortion; requiring price above its trend confirms the market is starting to agree with the value case. Screener.in substitutes DMA 50/200 for Chartink's sma().
O'Shaughnessy.exit: Exit if: composite valuation rank slips out of the cheapest 25% of the scan universe (re-rated fairly) · price closes below DMA 50 · EPS growth turns negative.
O'Shaughnessy.screen:
Market Capitalization > 500 AND
 Price to Sales > 0 AND
 Price to Sales < 1.5 AND
 Price to Earning > 0 AND
 Price to Earning < 20 AND
 Price to book value < 3 AND
 EPS > EPS preceding year AND
 Current price > DMA 50 AND
 DMA 50 > DMA 200

Pabrai / Dhandho.philosophy: Low-risk, high-uncertainty bets: cheap on book/earnings with genuine downside protection, not just statistical cheapness.
Pabrai / Dhandho.thesis: Low-risk, high-uncertainty special situations — structurally capped downside (asset backing, cheap-to-book) with a wide range of possible upside outcomes. Cheap on book value plus strong current profitability (Net Profit x multiple > Market Cap, an earnings-yield proxy) plus solid ROE confirms the downside is genuinely limited, not just statistically cheap.
Pabrai / Dhandho.exit: Exit if: Price to book value > 2.5 (downside-protection thesis played out) · OPM < 10 · Current ratio < 1.2 · stop-loss at -20% from entry.
Pabrai / Dhandho.screen:
Price to book value < 1.2 AND
 Current ratio > 1.5 AND
 Debt to equity < 0.4 AND
 Net profit * 15 > Market Capitalization AND
 OPM > 14 AND
 Return on equity > 10 AND
 Free cash flow last year > 0

Parag Parikh (PPFAS).philosophy: Value investing filtered through behavioral discipline: quality (ROE/ROCE) at reasonable prices with clean governance, avoiding herd-driven names.
Parag Parikh (PPFAS).thesis: Classic value investing filtered through behavioral discipline — avoid herd behavior, favor honest, high-ownership management at reasonable valuations. An ROE/ROCE quality gate plus PEG for "reasonable price" plus zero pledging as the governance/honesty proxy.
Parag Parikh (PPFAS).exit: Exit if: any pledge appears · PEG Ratio > 2 · Promoter holding < 30 · ROE < 12.

 Return on equity > 15 AND
 Return on capital employed > 15 AND
 Debt to equity < 0.5 AND
 Sales growth 5Years > 10 AND
 Promoter holding > 40 AND
 Pledged percentage = 0 AND
 PEG Ratio < 1.5 AND
 Price to Earning < 20

Peter Lynch.philosophy: Growth at a reasonable price: own understandable businesses with strong earnings growth relative to valuation and sound balance sheets, hunting for durable multi-year compounders.

Piotroski.philosophy: Cheap stocks whose balance sheets are genuinely healing — improving profitability, leverage, liquidity and efficiency YoY — not just statistically cheap.
Piotroski.thesis: A 9-point binary checklist (Piotroski, 2000, Journal of Accounting Research) that separates improving, financially sound value stocks from value traps — designed specifically for cheap stocks, not growth names. Score >=7 signals the balance sheet is genuinely healing (profitability, leverage, liquidity, and efficiency all improving YoY), not just cheap on paper.
Piotroski.exit: Exit if: Piotroski score < 5 in the next annual report · Current ratio < 1 · Cash from operations turns negative · position held beyond 18 months without a re-rating (Piotroski names are workouts, not forever-holds) · stop-loss at -20% from entry.
Piotroski.screen:
Piotroski score >= 7 AND
 Price to Sales < 3 AND
 Debt to equity < 1 AND
 Current ratio > 1.5 AND
 Interest Coverage Ratio > 3 AND
 Cash from operations last year > 0 AND
 Market Capitalization > 300 AND
 Price to Earning > 0 AND
 Price to Earning < 20

Porinju Veliyath.philosophy: Buy unloved small-caps cheap on both earnings and book value that are already showing an early operating recovery.
Porinju Veliyath.thesis: Unloved small-caps priced for pessimism that are already showing an early operating recovery — buy the inflection, not the story. Cheap on both earnings and book value simultaneously, with positive ROE confirming it is not a value trap that is actually losing money.
Porinju Veliyath.exit: Exit if: Price to book value > 3 (re-rating complete) · ROE turns negative any single quarter · Debt to equity > 1.5 · no earnings/OPM recovery visible after 4 reported quarters held · stop-loss at -25% from entry.
Porinju Veliyath.screen:
Market Capitalization < 5000 AND
 Price to Earning < 18 AND
 Price to book value < 2 AND
 Return on equity > 12 AND
 Return on capital employed > 12 AND
 Debt to equity < 1 AND
 Sales growth 3Years > 10 AND
 OPM > 10

QGLP (Raamdeo Agarwal).philosophy: Quality x Growth x Longevity bought at a reasonable price — growth only compounds value when ROCE clears the cost of capital.
QGLP (Raamdeo Agarwal).thesis: Quality x Growth x Longevity, bought at a reasonable Price. Growth only creates value when ROCE exceeds the cost of capital — growth without that spread destroys value. This is the one style with a live, reproducible public Screener.in formula matching your own "Claude" variant almost verbatim — kept intact, PEG as the reasonable-price gate.
QGLP (Raamdeo Agarwal).exit: Exit if: PEG Ratio > 1.5 · ROCE < 12 · Promoter holding < 40 · Profit growth 5Years < 5.
QGLP (Raamdeo Agarwal).screen:
Promoter holding > 50 AND
 Return on capital employed > 15 AND
 Sales growth 5Years > 10 AND
 Profit growth 5Years > 10 AND
 PEG Ratio < 1 AND
 Market Capitalization > 1000

Sanjay Bakshi.philosophy: Good businesses at sane (mid-range, not deep-value or glamour) valuations, with consistent high ROE/ROCE and moderate leverage.
Sanjay Bakshi.thesis: Blends Graham-style quantitative value with Munger-style qualitative moat/behavioral-bias checklists — best known for the "Behavioral Value Investing" case-study method. A mid-range PE band (not deep-value, not glamour) plus high, consistent ROE/ROCE across a full cycle plus moderate leverage — "a good business at a sane price," not a bargain bin.
Sanjay Bakshi.exit: Exit if: Average ROE 5Years < 12 · Debt to equity > 1.5 · Sales growth 7Years < 8 · Price to Earning > 35 without Profit growth 3Years rising above 15.
Sanjay Bakshi.screen:
Price to Earning > 12 AND
 Price to Earning < 28 AND
 Return on equity > 20 AND
 Average return on equity 5Years > 15 AND
 Return on capital employed > 20 AND
 Average return on capital employed 5Years > 15 AND
 Debt to equity < 1 AND
 Price to book value < 10 AND
 Sales growth 7Years > 15 AND
 Market Capitalization < 15000

Templeton.philosophy: Bargain-hunt in beaten-down, out-of-favor names that are cheap on sentiment rather than broken fundamentally.
Templeton.thesis: "Buy at the point of maximum pessimism" — bargain-hunt in beaten-down names trading well below historical/sector-normalized earnings multiples. PE below sector norm, price near its 52-week low, and positive non-deteriorating ROE together confirm the stock is cheap because of sentiment, not because the business is broken.
Templeton.exit: Exit if: price rises more than 40% above the 52-week low it was bought near (thesis largely realized) · ROE turns negative · Debt to equity > 1.5.
Templeton.screen:
Price to Earning < 0.6 * Industry PE AND
 Price to book value < 1.5 AND
 Return on equity > 10 AND
 Debt to equity < 1 AND
 Current price < 1.2 * Low price 52 weeks AND
 EPS last year > EPS preceding year

Terry Smith.philosophy: Own high-ROCE, low-capital-intensity businesses with pricing power at a sensible price, and hold with minimal churn.
Terry Smith.thesis: High-ROCE businesses with pricing power and low capital intensity, bought without overpaying, then held with minimal churn — resistant to macro-timing calls. Multi-horizon ROCE plus sales/profit growth consistency (3/5-year, all above 10-20) is the core; FCF yield versus market cap confirms real cash conversion, not accounting profit.
Terry Smith.exit: Exit if: ROCE 3Years average < 15 · FCF yield turns negative · Interest Coverage Ratio < 3.
Terry Smith.screen:
Return on capital employed > 20 AND
 Average return on capital employed 3Years > 20 AND
 Average return on capital employed 5Years > 20 AND
 OPM 5Year > 15 AND
 Interest Coverage Ratio > 5 AND
 (Free cash flow last year / Market Capitalization) * 100 > 5 AND
 Sales growth 3Years > 10 AND
 Profit growth 3Years > 10 AND
 Market Capitalization > 3000

Vijay Kedia.philosophy: Multibagger hunting in small/mid-caps with strong multi-year growth, high capital efficiency, and low leverage, held through the compounding cycle.
Vijay Kedia.screen: Market Capitalization > 500 AND Market Capitalization < 15000 AND Sales growth 5Years > 12 AND Profit growth 5Years > 15 AND Average return on capital employed 5Years > 18 AND Return on capital employed > 18 AND Return on equity > 15 AND Debt to equity < 0.5 AND Promoter holding > 40 AND Pledged percentage = 0

Zweig.philosophy: Buy stocks with accelerating quarter-over-quarter earnings growth while the P/E has not yet fully caught up to that growth rate.
Zweig.thesis: Buy accelerating quarter-over-quarter earnings at a P/E that has not yet caught up with the growth rate — momentum with a valuation leash, unlike pure CANSLIM. QoQ acceleration (this quarter beats last quarter's growth rate) is the core signal; a PE-to-growth ceiling keeps you out of names the market has already fully re-rated.
Zweig.exit: Exit if: QoQ profit growth decelerates for 2 consecutive quarters · Price to Earning crosses 1.5x Profit growth 3Years · Debt to equity > 0.75.

Damani.philosophy: Patiently hold capital-light, high-FCF category leaders with near-zero debt or pledging and multi-year ROCE consistency.
Damani.thesis: Extreme patience with capital-light, high free-cash-flow businesses that dominate their category; near-zero tolerance for leverage or promoter pledging. Multi-year (7Yr average) ROCE consistency rather than a single good year, plus a hard debt/pledge filter a genuinely conservative operator clears easily.
Damani.exit: Exit if: Pledged percentage > 0 (any pledge at all) · Debt to equity > 0.5 · ROCE 3Years average < 15 · OPM falls more than 300bps YoY without a disclosed one-off cause · stop-loss at -20% from entry.
